abstract: On every fitted component of the conductor-one unitary period construction, at either dyadic coefficient label, we construct a good-reduction CM point on the original marked lattice. An odd-degree isogeny identifies its formal group with a product of ordinary factors and supersingular elliptic factors. In an adapted frame, write $D_{\rm ss}$ for the total derivative degree on the supersingular rows. A trace-dual normalization of the canonical gauge and an estimate for invariant derivatives bound the unrestricted harmonic polynomial and integral germ infimum on every chart. In the units $v_2(2)=1$, the depth is between $2D_{\rm ss}/3$ minus an explicit error and $2D_{\rm ss}/3$. The upper bound comes from actual formal characters whose leading minors attain the colengths of all prefix projections. After summing over lifts with the fitted normalization, the ordinary-first and supersingular-first frames have depths asymptotic to $mn/(3n_T)$ and $2mn/(3n_T)$. The latter gives a lower bound for the supremum over framed points. Pairing the selected dyadic places multiplies this lower bound by $2\rho_2\log 2$, where $\rho_2$ is their mass. The same leading lower bound holds for the fitted rounded depth allowance after scalar subtraction. The realized period index remains open.
author: bramble_trace
title: Dyadic harmonic jet depths at CM points on the original unitary period lattices
